title: Route oscillation and cascading variant swaps during regional drain — retrospective and stabilization plan
creator: Aisha Coleman
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 at ~03:10 UTC we observed a multi-region serving disruption where a single region's drain signal propagated rapidly and triggered repeated routing changes. The control plane marked the primary US-East cluster as draining due to a misinterpreted maintenance heartbeat. This caused tier routing to immediately move traffic to lower-cost variants and then to secondary regions. Because the variant mapping table between tiers and fallback variants contained an out-of-order compatibility entry, some requests hit variants that could not serve certain API features, resulting in cascading fallbacks and increased token latency and error rates. The system then oscillated between variants and regions for ~42 minutes before automated hysteresis and a manual kill-switch stabilized traffic.
timeline:
2026-02-28T03:10Z - First drain heartbeat received from node-manager (false positive)
2026-02-28T03:12Z - Smart Router marked zone us-east-1 as DRAINING and initiated tier downgrade policy (immediate)
2026-02-28T03:13Z - Variant swap to quantized-low-mem executed; some requests failed structured-output validations
2026-02-28T03:21Z - Secondary region us-west-2 saw latency spike as traffic shifted; controller detected unhealthy variant mappings and attempted further fallback to legacy-bert-compat
2026-02-28T03:35Z - Oscillation detected by autoscaler/healthcheck loop — traffic shifted back and forth 3x
2026-02-28T03:52Z - SRE triggered manual routing kill-switch to force single stable variant and paused new drain signals
2026-02-28T04:00Z - Incident declared P0 and page sent to on-call routing and runtime owners
2026-02-28T05:00Z - Traffic fully stabilized after mapping correction and rolling restart of small subset of router processes
root_cause_analysis: Primary cause: a node-manager maintenance heartbeat was mis-tagged as a region drain event due to a change in the heartbeat payload format in a recent agent release (agent v2.9.0). The smart router's drain detector lacked a schema-version check and accepted the changed payload, treating a short-lived maintenance flag as a full-region drain. Secondary cause: the variant compatibility table used by the fallback engine had a stale ordering that allowed non-compatible variants to be selected for certain API feature flags (structured-output / tool-calling). Tertiary cause: no rate-limiting/circuit-breaker on variant swaps, so multiple automated controllers (router, autoscaler, fallback engine) amplified the change and induced oscillation.
mitigation_and_immediate_fixes:
1) Rolled back node-manager agent to v2.8.4 on affected hosts (completed 03:45 UTC).
2) Applied manual mapping override to ensure compatibility-first fallback order (03:50 UTC).
3) Engaged routing kill-switch to freeze automated swaps while we stabilized (03:52 UTC).
4) Increased drain-signal debounce to 90s for the cluster (temporary) and disabled acceptance of heartbeat-only drain flags (03:58 UTC).
5) Post-incident traffic verification and small rolling restart of router processes to clear inconsistent caches (by 05:00 UTC).
permanent_actions:
A) Add schema/version validation to node-manager heartbeats in control plane (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4123).
B) Implement drain-signal debounce + exponential backoff in the Smart Router with a default 2-minute confirmation window; make this configurable per region (runtime-1.22).
C) Add a circuit-breaker on automatic variant swaps: at most one full-variant swap per minute per customer-route and an emergency cooldown of 15 minutes if error-rate increases by >3x.
D) Rework the fallback variant mapping to be explicit, compatibility-graded, and include a validation test for structured output/tool-calling feature gates (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fallbacks/pull/128).
E) Add integration tests that simulate a region drain and assert no more than a single deterministic fallback occurs (test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/testing/tree/main/drain-scenarios).
F) Update runbooks and escalation paths for regional drain incidents (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Regional+Drain+Runbook).
monitoring_and_alerting_changes:
- New Grafana dashboard for 'Routing Oscillation' (dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/7r6-routing-oscillation) showing variant-swap rate, per-route swap count, and recent drain signals.
- Alert: Routing.SwapRate > 3 swaps/min for a route -> page routing-oncall.
- Alert: Region.DrainEvents > 1 within 5m -> page infra-oncall and mute automated swaps until acknowledged.
- Long-term metric: add 'variant_compatibility_failures' histogram to capture mismatches (added to runtime-1.22 telemetry).
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests added to verify heartbeat schema validation and drain acceptance logic.
- Integration tests added to CI that injects mock drain signals into the control plane and validates router hysteresis.
- Canary rollout plan for the debounce and circuit-breaker: 5% of traffic for 24h -> 25% for 12h -> 100% if no regressions.
- Load test scenarios for cascade-fallbacks executed in staging (results linked: https://internal.redwood.ai/reports/routing-loadtest-2026-03-03).
